Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. Vivek Pathak

Mr. Amar Shukla and Mr. B.M. Pingal, Advocates, for the

December 22, 2017

Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
The appeals titled above pertain to the same
property which is a plot no. 50 ad measuring 30 x 63 feet
in New Haridwar Colony. So, these are being taken up
together for hearing.
This Court has heard learned Senior Counsel on
behalf of the appellant Mr. Wadhwa as well as learned
Counsel of the caveator/respondent on the question of
admission and appreciated the facts at this stage itself.
After hearing learned Counsel for the parties, both appeals
are being finally decided at the admission stage itself on the
following substantial question of law:
ìWhether the rights of the parties have
not been substantially and effectively
decided on account of lapse on the part of
plaintiff by not producing himself for the
cross-examination in the witness box as
well as not producing any of the legal
heirs of Mr. Yashpal Wadhwa, the original
lease holder of the plot in question?î
The facts, as emerging out from the rival
contentions, are that there were two adjacent plots bearing
no. 49 and 50 at the place, which is of late called as New
Haridwar Colony and these have been within the municipal
limits and almost identically ad measuring. It is
undisputed that plot no. 49 was purchased by Doctor Ram
Ujagar Upadhyay and he sold the same in 1996. It seems

4
that the plot no. 50 was a vacant piece of land, which
somehow could be left as such while the colony was
developed by the power of attorney holder Chaudhary
Swaroop Singh on behalf of the owner Chaudhary Tek
Chand S/o Chaudhary Udai Ram. Chaudhary Swaroop
Singh granted the perpetual lease in favour of Mr. Ram Lal
R/o Bheem Gauda and from Ram Lal, this property was
inherited by his daughter Smt. Kamla Devi, who executed a
registered perpetual deed on 29.9.1965/9.7.1965 in favour
of the defendant/appellant Mr. Yashpal Wadhwa (now
deceased). It further appears that since Mr. Yashpal
Wadhwa used to reside in Delhi, hence taking advantage of
this position, Mr. Bhagwati Prasad Upadhyay, father of
Doctor Ram Ujagar Upadhyay, the owner of adjoining plot
no. 49, took the plot no. 50 in his adverse possession and
after waiting for few years, he got constructed a residential
accommodation on such piece of land and gave the same to
Mr. Shailendra as demised premises. Mr. Shailendra
accepting Mr. Bhagwati Prasad Upadhyay and thereafter
his son Doctor Ram Ujagar Upadhyay as the owners of the
said accommodation, used to pay the rent to them.
When the above state of affairs came to the
notice of Mr. Yashpal Wadhwa, he came first time on
26.4.1998 (as pleaded by the plaintiff Mr. Upadhyay) to
disturb his possession. So, the Original Suit No. 112/1998
was presented seeking the declaratory decree of ownership
as well as the direction restraining the defendants not to
interfere in his possession. That suit was previously
decreed ex parte on 26.5.2001, but later on such ex parte
decree was set aside and the suit was decreed on merits on
30.1.2014, whereagainst the Civil Appeal No. 16/2014 was
presented by Mr. Yashpal Wadhwa and it was also

5
dismissed vide judgment and order dated 29.5.2017, which
is impugned before this Court.
A parallel suit was also being proceeded as
Original Suit No. 77/2002 pleading that the cause of action
arose on 29.3.2002. In this suit, the decree of permanent
injunction was sought restraining the defendants not to
transfer the property, in question, or to create any third
party interest over it and not to recover the possession of
the same as well. Such suit was decided on merits and it
was dismissed on 11.7.2013 by the Additional Civil Judge
(Jr. Div.), Haridwar, whereagainst the Civil Appeal No.
51/2013 was preferred, which was allowed by the same
Additional District Judge on the same date 29.5.2017.
It is undisputed that Doctor Ram Ujagar
Upadhyay, though got his chief examination recorded in
the Original Suit No. 77/2002 but he never turned up in
the witness box to face the cross-examination. On the other
hand, Mr. Yashpal Wadhwa could not put his appearance
because of his death. After his death, none of his legal heirs
as well could muster the courage to appear in the witness
box to record the chief examination or the cross-examination, while simply a power of attorney Mr. Nand
Lal, who is also a resident of Delhi but presently resides in
Haridwar, could appear but he was not aware about the
details and the facts of the lease deed in favour of Mr.
Yashpal Wadhwa and such facts could have been adverted
only by producing either of the legal heirs and pre-dominantly Smt. Usha Wadhwa in the witness box and
more so, when the certified copy of such perpetual lease
was presented during the appellate stage. So, the plaintiff
did not get any opportunity to cross-examine the defendant
witness on the facts and particularly on that lease deed.

6
The claim of Doctor Upadhyay was decreed by
the Appellate Court just on the basis of municipal entries
and electricity and water connections, which cannot have
any bearing to decide the ownership of the land.
Substantial question of law is answered
accordingly.
In view of what has been set forth above, I set
aside both the impugned judgments passed by the Trial
Court as well as the Appellate Court and remand the
matters to the Trial Court for deciding the same de novo
compelling Doctor Ram Ujagar Upadhyay as well as any of
the legal heirs of Mr. Yashpal Wadhwa having the
knowledge about the lease deed to appear in the witness
box. Both the Original Suits shall remain consolidated
together for recording the evidence.
Till the Original Suits are decided finally and the
rights of the parties are adjudicated, status quo shall be
maintained by the parties over the property, in question,
and they shall also not create any third party interest, in
any manner, over the same.
LCRs be sent back.
